newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan trade surplus still on declining trend--MOF.
newsitem.headline: Japan trade surplus still on declining trend--MOF.

text.p: Japan's trade surplus is still on a declining trend, a Ministry of Finance official told reporters on Thursday.
However, asked if the pace of the decline had slowed -- something the ministry has asserted in previous months -- the official said: "It is difficult to tell."
The ministry earlier announced that Japan's unadjusted customs-cleared trade surplus fell 20.6 percent in December compared with the year before to 881.48 billion yen.

Discussing the pace of decline, he said that exports of cars were high, a reaction from low levels last year and this trend would continue for a while. Car exports rose 13.4 percent year-on-year in December.
But he added that oil imports rose 59.4 percent in December from a year earlier. He said although oil imports only rose 7.3 percent in volume terms, they rose 48.4 percent in value terms.
The official also said that the trade surplus' declining trend had not been interrupted despite preliminary numbers for November showing a year-on-year rise in the surplus of 0.2 percent.

He said revised figures showed a 0.4 percent decline in the surplus to 670.77 billion yen for November. He said there were no special factors in the revisions, adding that some exports originally planned had been cancelled and that value of some imports had been revised.
